items.raw_excerpt: Successive rises in fuel prices are placing increasing pressure on Portugal’s fire brigades, with some associations already facing cash-flow problems.
items.summary_en: Successive rises in fuel prices are putting increasing pressure on Portugal's volunteer fire brigades. Some local fire associations are already facing serious cash-flow problems and struggling to keep operating.

items.summary_en: Italian teacher and YouTuber Lucrezia Oddone shares common struggles people face when learning Italian. She offers practical strategies for newcomers to Italy or anyone hoping to move there someday. Her advice is simple and encouraging for beginners.

items.raw_excerpt: Norway has released its first national guidelines on screen use for children and young people from birth to 18 years old. Here’s what parents should keep in mind to protect your kids, from tiny toddlers to teens.
items.summary_en: Norway has released its first national guidelines on screen use for children and young people from birth to 18 years old. The rules set limits on how much time children should spend on screens at different ages. Parents are urged to follow the new advice to protect kids' health and wellbeing.

items.title_en: Norway sets first national screen time limits for children from birth to 18

items.summary_en: Workers at Taiwanese snack maker Kuai Kuai protested outside the Presidential Office demanding compensation. The company sold its factory site in Taoyuan's Zhongli District and plans to relocate to Hsinchu.

items.raw_excerpt: This French expression can be used in both serious and light-hearted contexts.
items.summary_en: The Local France shares a daily French expression. "Perdre la raison" means to lose one's mind. It can be used in both serious and light-hearted situations.

items.raw_excerpt: We don't want to be a Cassandra, but you really should believe us about this phrase.
items.summary_en: Fare la Cassandra means to warn people about a coming problem or disaster. It comes from Cassandra of Greek mythology, who made true bad predictions that nobody believed. Italians use it when someone keeps warning about bad things to come.
items.summary_ko: '카산드라 하기'는 곧 닥칠 문제나 재난을 미리 경고한다는 뜻입니다. 이름은 그리스 신화에서 맞는 불길한 예언을 했지만 아무도 믿지 않은 카산드라에게서 나왔습니다. 이탈리아인들은 누군가 앞으로 일어날 안 좋은 일을 계속 경고할 때 이 표현을 씁니다.
items.title_en: Italian expression of the day: 'Fare la Cassandra'
items.title_original: Italian expression of the day: 'Fare la Cassandra'

items.raw_excerpt: Ready to start speaking Dutch? The Dutch Brainwash school, which sponsored this piece, invited DutchNews’ Lauren Comiteau to visit a class. On the sweltering August day I visit Albert Both’s Brainwash class on the Keizersgracht in the heart of the Jordaan, you can hear the laughter before you even enter the room. During this last class of Both’s current one-week intensive Dutch language course, eight students – Both’s maximum per course – sit around a huge white table that takes...
items.summary_en: A small language school in Amsterdam offers intensive one-week Dutch courses. Students learn through conversation and games in a cozy classroom on the Keizersgracht canal. The school keeps classes to just eight students to make learning personal and fun.
items.summary_ko: 암스테르담의 작은 어학원이 일주일 집중 네덜란드어 과정을 운영합니다. 학생들은 케이저스그라트 운변의 아늑한 교실에서 대화와 게임을 통해 언어를 배웁니다. 수업은 학생 8명으로 제한되어 개인적이고 재미있는 학습 환경을 만듭니다.
items.title_en: Brainwash: Anatomy of a Dutch language course
items.title_original: Brainwash: Anatomy of a Dutch language course

items.raw_excerpt: From the hockey rink to the political arena, the phrase “Elbows Up” has become part of the Canadian lexicon — and now a number of businesses are trying to cash in on it.
items.summary_en: The phrase 'Elbows Up' started as a hockey expression. It is now a famous patriotic phrase across Canada. Many businesses are cashing in by selling products that use the slogan.

items.title_en: 'Elbows Up' slogan becomes a chance for Canadian businesses

items.raw_excerpt: Planned Icelandic state fee increases could be scaled back as the government negotiates with labour and employer representatives.
items.summary_en: Iceland's government is negotiating with labour unions and employer groups over planned state fee increases for 2027. The Prime Minister says the hikes may be scaled back after those talks. The changes could affect how much residents pay in various public fees.

items.title_en: PM says planned state fee hikes could be reduced
